topic: Coronary Arteries: circle and loop
stem: In the circle-and-loop concept of coronary artery anatomy, which pair of arteries forms the **loop** that encircles the ventricular septum?

choices.text: Right coronary and left circumflex arteries
Left main and left circumflex arteries
Left anterior descending and posterior descending arteries
Left anterior descending and left circumflex arteries
Right coronary and acute marginal arteries

explanation.text: The **loop** = **left anterior descending** (in front) + **posterior descending** artery (behind), encircling the septum at right angles to the circle.

explanation.title: Why the loop matters
explanation.text: The ventricular septum receives its blood supply from the loop that encircles it: **LAD in front**, **posterior descending artery behind**.

The loop between the ventricles and at right angles to the circle is formed by the left anterior descending (interventricular) coronary artery and the posterior descending (interventricular) coronary artery as they encircle the septum.

choiceNotes.a: These two form the **circle**, as they traverse the AV sulci, not the loop.
choiceNotes.b: The left main ends by bifurcating into the LAD and circumflex; the circumflex is the left part of the **circle**.
choiceNotes.d: The LAD is part of the loop, but the circumflex forms the left component of the **circle**.
choiceNotes.e: The acute marginal is an RCA branch at the acute margin; the loop is formed by the two interventricular (descending) arteries.

topic: Coronary Arteries: circle and loop
stem: On the coronary angiograms of Fig. 1.27, the circle and the loop of the coronary arteries are each displayed in a particular projection. Which pairing is correct?

choices.text: Circle in the LAO projection; loop in the RAO projection
Circle in the RAO projection; loop in the LAO projection
Circle and loop both in the LAO projection
Circle and loop both in the RAO projection

explanation.text: **Circle -> LAO**, **Loop -> RAO** (Fig. 1.27).

head: Panel
Injection / view
What it shows
rows: RCA = right component of the circle (right dominant)
Left circumflex = left component of the circle (left dominant)

explanation.title: Panel C
explanation.text: In panel C (left coronary injection, **RAO**), the **left dominant** circulation allows demonstration of **both components of the loop**: LAD and posterior descending artery.

Circle is formed by right coronary and left circumflex arteries and is displayed in the LAO projection. Loop is formed by left anterior descending and posterior descending arteries and is demonstrated in the right anterior oblique (RAO) projection.

choiceNotes.b: Reversed: the circle (RCA + circumflex) is displayed in **LAO**, the loop (LAD + PDA) in **RAO**.
choiceNotes.c: LAO displays the circle; the loop is demonstrated in **RAO**.
choiceNotes.d: RAO demonstrates the loop; the circle is displayed in **LAO**.

topic: Coronary Arteries: right coronary artery
stem: In a heart with a right dominant circulation, the extension of the right coronary artery across the crux, along the posterior AV groove, that gives inferior surface (marginal) branches to the diaphragmatic surface of the left ventricle is termed the:

choices.text: Acute marginal artery
Posterior descending artery
Left AV artery
Right posterolateral segment
Atrial circumflex artery

explanation.text: Beyond the crux, a right dominant RCA continues in the AV groove as the **right posterolateral segment**, which sends marginal branches to the **inferior (diaphragmatic) surface of the LV**.
**Crux cordis**: the area along the posterior aspect of the AV groove where the **atrial and ventricular septa meet**.

branches.label: groove
branches.text: **Right posterolateral segment** -> inferior surface branches to the back of the LV

explanation.title: Right dominant RCA at the crux
Right dominant does not guarantee inferior LV branches
explanation.text: A right dominant artery may terminate **only as the posterior descending artery**, giving no branches to the inferior LV surface.

the extension of the right coronary artery across the crux cordis, the area along the posterior aspect of the AV groove where the atrial and ventricular septa meet, termed the right posterolateral segment.

choiceNotes.a: The acute marginal arises at the **acute margin** and courses most of the way to the apex.
choiceNotes.b: The PDA descends in the **posterior interventricular sulcus**; at the crux the RCA bifurcates into the PDA **and** the right posterolateral segment artery.
choiceNotes.c: The left AV artery is the extension of the **circumflex**, present only in **left dominant** systems.
choiceNotes.e: The atrial circumflex artery arises from the proximal **left circumflex** and courses around the left atrium.

topic: Coronary Arteries: right coronary artery
stem: In terms of the number and volume of vessel segments involved, which statement best describes the territory of the right coronary artery?

choices.text: It serves the right side of the heart more than the left side
It serves the left side of the heart more than the right side
It serves only the right atrium and right ventricle
It serves both sides equally in a right dominant heart
It serves the left ventricle only in a left dominant heart

explanation.text: Even if it does not supply a large portion of the posterior LV wall, the **RCA serves the left side of the heart more than the right side** (number and volume of vessel segments).

items: **Right posterolateral segment** -> marginal branches to the inferior surface of the LV (most right dominant hearts)
**Posterior descending artery** -> septal, right ventricular **and left ventricular** branches

explanation.title: Right dominant is not the same as inferior LV supply
explanation.text: A right dominant artery may terminate **only as the posterior descending artery**, without branches to the inferior LV surface.
it nevertheless serves the left side of the heart to a greater extent than it does the right side in terms of the number and volume of vessel segments involved.

choiceNotes.a: The reverse: the source says it serves the **left** side to a greater extent.
choiceNotes.c: Its posterolateral segment supplies the inferior LV surface in most right dominant hearts, and its PDA gives left ventricular and septal branches.
choiceNotes.d: Not equally: the left side is served **to a greater extent** than the right.
choiceNotes.e: In a left dominant heart the posterior descending artery and inferior LV branches come from the **circumflex**.

topic: Coronary Arteries: circle and loop
stem: According to the circle-loop description of left ventricular blood supply, the **lateral part of the anterior portion** of the left ventricle is supplied by:

choices.text: Diagonal branches of the LAD alone
Obtuse marginal arteries from the posterior half of the circle
Septal branches of the posterior descending artery
Inferior surface branches of the right posterolateral segment
First branches of both the LAD and the left circumflex arteries

explanation.text: **Lateral part of the anterior LV** = first branches of **both** the LAD **and** the circumflex.

head: LV region
Supplied by
rows: **First branches of both LAD and circumflex**
Parallel **obtuse marginal** arteries from the posterior half of the circle
Inferior surface (marginal) branches of the **right posterolateral segment** (right dominant)
explanation.caption: Left ventricular blood supply (circle-loop view)

explanation.title: Posterior half of the circle
explanation.text: Formed on the left by the **left circumflex** and on the right (right dominant hearts) by the **right posterolateral segment**.
that to the lateral part of the anterior portion comes from the first branches of both the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries.

choiceNotes.a: Diagonals of the LAD supply the **anterior** portion of the LV; its **lateral** part also receives the first circumflex branches.
choiceNotes.b: These parallel obtuse marginal arteries supply the **back** of the LV.
choiceNotes.c: PDA septal arteries supply only a small zone of the septum near the posterior interventricular sulcus and the AV node region.
choiceNotes.d: These branches supply the **inferior (diaphragmatic)** surface of the LV.

topic: Coronary Arteries: dominance
stem: In coronary anatomy, the term **dominance** expresses variability in which feature?

choices.text: The origin of the posterior descending artery
The origin of the sinus node artery
The relative caliber of the two coronary ostia
The length of the left main coronary artery
The artery that supplies the AV node

explanation.text: **Dominance** = which artery gives rise to the **posterior descending artery (PDA)**.

head: Pattern
PDA arises from
rows: **Terminal branch** of the right coronary artery
A branch, **usually the last one**, of the left circumflex

explanation.title: Why surgeons care
explanation.text: Whether the right or left coronary artery supplies the PDA is important in **evaluating coronary artery disease** and in **planning CABG**.

explanation.title: Consequence, not definition
explanation.text: The AV node is **usually** supplied by the dominant coronary artery, but dominance itself is defined only by the PDA origin.
Variability in the origin of the posterior descending artery is expressed by the term dominance.

choiceNotes.b: The sinus node artery origin (right coronary in 55% to 65%) is not what defines dominance.
choiceNotes.c: Dominance is defined by the origin of the PDA, not by vessel size.
choiceNotes.d: Left main length (usually 10 to 20 mm) is unrelated to dominance.
choiceNotes.e: The AV node is **usually** supplied by the dominant artery, a consequence of dominance, not its definition.

source.loc: p. 22, Coronary Arterial Supply to Specialized Areas of the Heart

topic: Coronary Arteries: dominance
stem: Angiography before coronary artery bypass grafting shows the posterior descending artery arising as the last branch of the left circumflex artery. Which statement about this pattern is correct?

choices.text: It is the usual pattern, present in most hearts
It is more frequent in females than in males
It occurs in about 10% to 15% of hearts, more often in males
The ventricular septum still receives part of its supply from the RCA
It occurs in about 1% of hearts

explanation.text: PDA from the circumflex = **left dominant** circulation: about **10% to 15%** of hearts, **more frequent in males**.

children: PDA is a branch, usually the last, of the left circumflex
about 10% to 15% of hearts
more frequent in males than females
at or usually before the crux
entire blood supply from the left coronary artery

explanation.title: Surgical relevance
explanation.text: Knowing whether the right or left artery supplies the PDA is important in **evaluating coronary artery disease** and **planning CABG**.

A left dominant circulation, which occurs in about 10% to 15% of hearts, is one in which the posterior descending coronary artery is a branch, usually the last one, of the left circumflex coronary artery.

choiceNotes.a: Left dominance occurs in only about **10% to 15%** of hearts.
choiceNotes.b: The reverse: left dominance is **more frequent in males**.
choiceNotes.d: In left dominant hearts the **entire** septal blood supply is from the **left** coronary artery (p. 21).
choiceNotes.e: About 1% is the frequency of an **absent left main** coronary artery.

source.loc: p. 21, Coronary Arterial Supply to Specialized Areas of the Heart

topic: Coronary Arteries: left circumflex artery
stem: In a codominant system in which the right coronary artery gives rise only to a posterior descending artery, the circumflex branches that supply the inferior surface of the left ventricle are termed:

choices.text: Right posterolateral arteries
Diagonal arteries
Atrial circumflex arteries
Acute marginal arteries
Left posterolateral arteries

explanation.text: Circumflex branches to the **inferior LV surface** (left dominant **or** codominant with an RCA that gives only a PDA) = **left posterolateral (marginal) arteries**.

head: System
PDA from
Inferior LV surface branches
rows: **Right** posterolateral arteries, from the right posterolateral segment (most hearts)
Circumflex, at or usually before the crux
**Left** posterolateral arteries from the **left AV artery**

explanation.title: Left AV artery (Fig. 1.28)
explanation.text: The extension of the circumflex present **only in left dominant systems**; it gives left posterolateral arteries before ending as the left posterior descending artery.

Those branches supplying the inferior surface of the left ventricle in a heart with a left dominant system (or in one with a codominant system in which the right coronary artery gives rise only to a posterior descending artery) are termed left posterolateral (marginal) arteries.

choiceNotes.a: Right posterolateral arteries come from the **right** posterolateral segment of a right dominant RCA.
choiceNotes.b: Diagonals are LAD branches supplying the LV free wall anteriorly and laterally.
choiceNotes.c: The atrial circumflex is a large proximal circumflex branch coursing around the **left atrium**.
choiceNotes.d: The acute marginal is a right coronary branch at the acute margin of the heart.

topic: Coronary Arteries: left main coronary artery
stem: The left main coronary artery arises from its ostium in the left sinus of Valsalva. To reach the left AV groove, it normally courses between:

choices.text: The aorta and the superior vena cava
The pulmonary trunk and the left atrial appendage
The pulmonary trunk and the right atrial appendage
The left atrial appendage and the left pulmonary veins
The aorta and the right ventricular infundibulum

explanation.text: Left main: **left sinus of Valsalva** -> between the **pulmonary trunk** and the **left atrial appendage** -> **left AV groove**.

children: ostium in the left sinus of Valsalva
between pulmonary trunk and left atrial appendage
reaches the left AV groove
usually 10 to 20 mm
range 0 to 40 mm
bifurcates into LAD and left circumflex

explanation.title: What follows
explanation.text: The **left circumflex** leaves the left main at about **90 degrees**, its first few centimeters lying **medial to the base of the left atrial appendage**.
It normally courses between the pulmonary trunk and the left atrial appendage to reach the left AV groove.

choiceNotes.a: The superior vena cava is where the **sinus node artery** ends; the left main runs between the pulmonary trunk and the left atrial appendage.
choiceNotes.c: The right atrial appendage is related to the **sinus node artery** from the RCA, not to the left main.
choiceNotes.d: The source places the left main between the **pulmonary trunk** and the left atrial appendage.
choiceNotes.e: The infundibulum is supplied by infundibular branches of the proximal RCA or a separate conus artery; the source places the left main between the pulmonary trunk and the left atrial appendage.

topic: Coronary Arteries: left main coronary artery
stem: Coronary angiography shows the left anterior descending and left circumflex arteries arising directly from the aorta through separate ostia. This finding represents:

choices.text: Dual origin of the right coronary artery from the right sinus
A conus artery arising separately from the aortic sinus
A left dominant coronary circulation
Absence of the left main coronary artery
A first diagonal branch arising from the left main

explanation.text: Separate aortic ostia for the LAD and circumflex = **absent left main coronary artery**, rare (**1%** of persons).

head: Left main finding
Meaning
rows: One left main, 10 to 20 mm (range 0 to 40 mm), bifurcating into LAD and circumflex
**First diagonal** of the LAD (formerly ramus intermedius)
**LAD and circumflex from separate aortic ostia**

explanation.title: Do not call it dominance
explanation.text: **Dominance** refers only to which artery gives rise to the posterior descending artery.
Rarely (in 1% of persons), the left main coronary artery is absent, with the left anterior descending and left circumflex coronary arteries originating directly from the aorta via separate ostia.

choiceNotes.a: Dual origin from the right sinus is a variation of the **right** coronary artery.
choiceNotes.b: The conus artery is the separately arising artery to the **right ventricular infundibulum**.
choiceNotes.c: Dominance describes the origin of the **posterior descending artery**, not separate LAD and circumflex ostia.
choiceNotes.e: The first diagonal (formerly ramus intermedius) is an **additional** vessel from an existing left main.

topic: Coronary Arteries: left main coronary artery
stem: An additional vessel originates from the left main coronary artery near its bifurcation. Formerly called the ramus intermedius, this artery is now termed the:

choices.text: First diagonal branch of the LAD
First obtuse marginal branch of the circumflex
Atrial circumflex artery
First septal branch of the LAD
Left AV artery

explanation.text: The old **ramus intermedius** is now called the **first diagonal branch** of the LAD.

head: Branch
Origin
Course / territory
rows: Parallel to the diagonals; obtuse margin between diagonal and circumflex marginal branches
Obliquely between LAD and circumflex; LV free wall anteriorly and laterally
Almost perpendicular, into the ventricular septum

explanation.title: Figure clue
explanation.text: Fig. 1.28 labels it segment **15**: the first diagonal, which may originate near the left main bifurcation.
Such an additional artery (formerly called a ramus intermedius) is termed the first diagonal branch of the left anterior descending artery.

choiceNotes.b: Obtuse marginals are **ventricular branches of the circumflex** supplying the obtuse margin.
choiceNotes.c: The atrial circumflex arises from the proximal circumflex and courses around the **left atrium**.
choiceNotes.d: Septal arteries leave the LAD almost perpendicularly and course **into the septum**.
choiceNotes.e: The left AV artery is the circumflex extension present only in **left dominant** systems.

topic: Coronary Arteries: left anterior descending artery
stem: In most hearts, the left anterior descending artery does not stop at the apex but extends around it into the posterior interventricular sulcus. As a result, it supplies:

choices.text: The posteromedial papillary muscle of the left ventricle
The apical portion of the left ventricle only
The apical portion of both the right and left ventricles
The inferior left ventricular surface via posterolateral branches
The AV node via short posterior septal branches

explanation.text: Wrapping around the apex, the LAD supplies the **apical portion of both ventricles**.

children: continuation of the left main
anterior interventricular sulcus -> apex
usually around the apex into the posterior sulcus
part may be buried in muscle
right ventricular free wall (usually small)
septum
left ventricular free wall
apical portion of right and left ventricles

explanation.title: Part of the loop
explanation.text: Running in the anterior sulcus, the LAD is the front half of the **loop** that encircles the septum.
In most cases, this artery extends around the apex into the posterior interventricular sulcus, supplying the apical portion of both right and left ventricles.

choiceNotes.a: The posteromedial papillary muscle is supplied by terminal branches of the **right or circumflex** arteries.
choiceNotes.b: Not only the LV: the source says the apical portion of **both** ventricles.
choiceNotes.d: Posterolateral branches to the inferior LV come from the right posterolateral segment or the circumflex.
choiceNotes.e: Short septal arteries near the AV node come from the **posterior descending** artery.

topic: Coronary Arteries: left anterior descending artery
stem: One or more right ventricular branches of the left anterior descending artery connect with infundibular branches from the proximal right coronary artery. This important route for collateral flow is the:

choices.text: Kugel artery
Right superior descending artery
Circle of the AV sulci
Atrial circumflex artery
Loop of Vieussens

explanation.text: LAD right ventricular branches <-> proximal RCA infundibular branches = **loop of Vieussens**, an important collateral route.

explanation.title: Another collateral source
explanation.text: The short **septal arteries of the posterior descending artery** may also serve as an important source of collateral circulation.
One or more branches to the right ventricle connect with infundibular branches from the proximal right coronary artery. This important route for collateral flow is the loop of Vieussens.

choiceNotes.a: The Kugel artery runs through the interatrial septum to the crux and anastomoses with the **AV node artery**.
choiceNotes.b: The right superior descending artery is an atrial vessel from the first centimeter of the RCA that supplies the **His bundle and AV node**.
choiceNotes.c: The circle is the RCA plus circumflex in the AV sulci, not an infundibular collateral.
choiceNotes.d: The atrial circumflex is a proximal circumflex branch coursing around the **left atrium**.

source.loc: p. 20, Left Anterior Descending Coronary Artery
p. 21, Coronary Arterial Supply to Specialized Areas of the Heart

topic: Coronary Arteries: left anterior descending artery
stem: On angiography, which feature is described as sometimes helpful in identifying the left anterior descending artery?

choices.text: A deep U-turn as it crosses the crux
Septal arteries arising almost perpendicularly from it
Origin at about a 90-degree angle from the left main
Branches that exit the AV sulcus in a looping fashion
A long branch running along the acute margin

explanation.text: **Septal arteries leave the LAD almost perpendicularly**: a sign that helps identify the LAD on angiography.

head: Septal arteries
Diagonal arteries
rows: On the surface, between LAD and circumflex
LV free wall, anteriorly and laterally

head: Artery
Recognizable feature
rows: Leaves the left main at about 90 degrees; first few cm medial to the left atrial appendage base
Deep U-turn at the crux; looping exit of RV branches from the AV sulcus
explanation.caption: Quick identification

explanation.text: The septal arteries arise almost perpendicularly from the left anterior descending coronary artery, a characteristic sometimes helpful in angiographic identification of the anterior descending artery.

choiceNotes.a: The deep U-turn at the crux is characteristic of the **right coronary artery**.
choiceNotes.c: The **left circumflex** originates from the left main at about 90 degrees.
choiceNotes.d: RCA branches to the anterior RV free wall loop out of the AV sulcus because of the artery's depth in it.
choiceNotes.e: The acute marginal is a long, relatively constant **RCA** branch.

topic: Coronary Arteries: left anterior descending artery
stem: Which variation is described for the **left anterior descending** artery?

choices.text: Dual origin from the right sinus of Valsalva
Early bifurcation into two diverging trunks near its ostium
Termination before the obtuse margin of the heart
Existence as two parallel vessels of about equal size
Origin of the sinus node artery from its first few millimeters

explanation.text: LAD variations are **infrequent**; in about **4%** of hearts it exists as **two parallel vessels of about equal size**.

head: Artery
Described variations
rows: Two parallel equal vessels (about 4%); may end before the apex or reach the posterior AV groove
Absent in 1% (separate LAD and circumflex ostia)
Rarely ends before the obtuse margin; may give the sinus node artery; origin, length and marginals vary often
Dual origin from the right sinus; early bifurcation into two equal trunks (about 10%); separate conus artery (half)

explanation.title: Common vs infrequent
explanation.text: Variations of the **circumflex** and **right coronary** arteries are **common**; those of the **LAD** are **infrequent**.
Variations in the left anterior descending artery are infrequent, although in about 4% of hearts, it exists as two parallel vessels of about equal size.

choiceNotes.a: Dual origin from the right sinus is described for the **right coronary artery**.
choiceNotes.b: Bifurcation within a few millimeters of the ostium into two equal trunks is an **RCA** variation (about 10% of hearts).
choiceNotes.c: Rare termination before the obtuse margin is described for the **left circumflex**.
choiceNotes.e: The sinus node artery occasionally arises from the first few millimeters of the **left circumflex**.

source.loc: p. 20, Left Anterior Descending Coronary Artery

choices.text: Left AV artery
First obtuse marginal artery
Left posterolateral artery
Right superior descending artery
Atrial circumflex artery

explanation.text: Proximal circumflex branch running **around the left atrium near the AV groove** = **atrial circumflex artery**.

A large branch originating from the proximal left circumflex artery and coursing around the left atrium near the AV groove is termed the atrial circumflex artery.

choiceNotes.a: The left AV artery is the **distal** extension of the circumflex in left dominant systems.
choiceNotes.b: Obtuse marginals are **ventricular** branches supplying the obtuse margin.
choiceNotes.c: Left posterolateral arteries supply the **inferior surface of the LV**.
choiceNotes.d: The right superior descending artery arises within the first centimeter of the **right** coronary artery.

topic: Coronary Arteries: left circumflex artery

choices.text: Altered color (reddish or light tan) of the thin overlying muscle
Its position medial to the base of the left atrial appendage
Septal branches leaving it at an almost perpendicular angle
A characteristic deep U-turn along its course on the LV
Branches leaving the AV sulcus in a looping fashion

explanation.text: A buried obtuse marginal is found by the **altered color (reddish or light tan)** of the thin muscle layer over it, compared with the rest of the ventricular wall.

items: **Obtuse marginal arteries** = ventricular branches of the circumflex
They supply the **obtuse margin** of the heart
Clue at operation: **color change** of the overlying thin muscle

explanation.title: Buried vessels elsewhere
explanation.text: Part of the **LAD** may also be buried in muscle.
Often their position can then be identified at operation by the altered color (reddish or light tan) of the overlying thin muscle layer compared with that of the remainder of the ventricular wall.

choiceNotes.b: The **initial few centimeters of the circumflex itself** lie medial to the base of the left atrial appendage.
choiceNotes.c: Almost perpendicular septal branches identify the **LAD** on angiography.
choiceNotes.d: The deep U-turn is made by the **right coronary artery** at the crux.

topic: Coronary Arterial Supply to Specialized Areas
stem: In a heart with a right dominant circulation, from which part of the right coronary artery does the AV node artery arise?

choices.text: The anterior right atrial artery near the atrial appendage
The apex of the deep U-turn as the artery crosses the crux
The second or third centimeter of the artery
The acute marginal artery at the acute margin
The right posterior descending artery near the apex

explanation.text: The **AV node artery** arises from the **apex of the deep U-turn** that the RCA makes as it crosses the **crux**.

steps.text: **AV node artery** from the apex of the turn: courses superiorly and anteriorly, ends with a distinctive angulation

explanation.title: Rule of thumb
explanation.text: The AV node is **usually supplied by the dominant coronary artery**.

explanation.title: PDA origin varies
explanation.text: The posterior descending artery **frequently arises before the crux**; its anatomy has numerous variations.
The right coronary artery in most hearts crosses the crux, where it takes a characteristic deep U-turn, giving off the AV node artery at the apex of the turn.

choiceNotes.a: The anterior right atrial artery often gives origin to the **sinus node** artery.
choiceNotes.c: The **sinus node** artery originates from the second or third centimeter of the RCA in many hearts.
choiceNotes.d: The acute marginal courses toward the apex and does not supply the AV node.

topic: Coronary Arteries: right coronary artery
stem: In 10% to 20% of hearts, which branch of the right coronary artery crosses the diaphragmatic surface of the right ventricle and reaches the anterior aspect of the diaphragmatic portion of the ventricular septum, to which it gives branches?

choices.text: Conus artery
Posterior descending artery
Right posterolateral segment artery
Acute marginal artery
Anterior right atrial artery

explanation.text: The **acute marginal artery** can cross the RV diaphragmatic surface and reach the diaphragmatic septum (**10% to 20%** of hearts).

items: Arises in the region of the **acute margin** of the heart
Courses **most of the way to the apex**
Other RCA branches to the RV are simply called **right ventricular branches**
10% to 20%: reaches and supplies the **diaphragmatic portion of the septum**

explanation.title: An extra septal source
explanation.text: Most septal supply is from LAD septals; PDA septals supply a small zone near the posterior sulcus, and in 10% to 20% of hearts the acute marginal also gives septal branches.

The acute marginal artery crosses the diaphragmatic surface of the right ventricle in 10% to 20% of hearts and reaches the anterior aspect of the diaphragmatic portion of the ventricular septum, to which it gives branches.

choiceNotes.a: The conus artery supplies the right ventricular **infundibulum**.
choiceNotes.b: The PDA descends in the **posterior interventricular sulcus**; the branch described crossing the RV diaphragmatic surface is the acute marginal.

explanation.title: Left dominant hearts
explanation.text: In hearts with a **left dominant** circulation, the **entire** blood supply of the septum is from the **left** coronary artery.
The predominant blood supply to the ventricular septum is from the left anterior descending coronary artery via four to six large septal arteries 70 to 80 mm in length.
